                "headline": "Special Marine Warning issued April 8 at 6:10PM EDT until April 8 at 7:15PM EDT by NWS Miami FL",
                "description": "SMWMFL\n\nThe National Weather Service in Miami has issued a\n\n* Special Marine Warning for...\nBiscayne Bay...\nCoastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...\nCoastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20\nNM...\nWaters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM\nexcluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...\nWaters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM...\n\n* Until 715 PM EDT.\n\n* At 610 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing\nwaterspouts were located along a line extending from 17 nm east of\nHighland Beach to near Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, moving south at 30\nknots.\n\nHAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.\n\nSOURCE...Radar.\n\nIMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally\nhazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly\nhigher winds and suddenly higher waves.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nSunny Isles, Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, Hallandale, Lighthouse Point,\nHillsboro Beach, Gulf Stream, Bay Harbor Islands, Delray Beach,\nPort Everglades, Miami Beach, Boca Raton, Highland Beach, Sea Ranch\nLakes, Bal Harbour, Golden Beach, Surfside, Briny Breezes, Indian\nCreek, Pompano Beach, and Ocean Ridge.",
                "instruction": "Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily\noverturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor\nimmediately.\n\nReport severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather\nService. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook\nand Twitter.",

Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain\nhave fallen.\n- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over\nthe area.                 "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued April 9 at 7:29AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU",
                "description": "Over the past 24 hours, Invest 90W has shown an improved convective\nsignature with good poleward outflow aloft (a sign that the system\nmay be strengthening). As such, the Joint Typhoon Warning Center has\nupgraded Invest 90W to a TCFA (Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert),\nmeaning the formation of a tropical cyclone (tropical depression\nstrength or stronger) is likely within the next 24 hours. Overall,\nthe models continue to showN a gradually strengthening system the\nnext several days, with current forecast tracks taking the system\nthrough western Chuuk State and eastern to east central Yap State,\nwith a passage south of Guam.\n\nThis will likely bring locally heavy rainfall, sustained winds of 35\nknots or more (with higher gusts), and an increasingly hazardous sea\nstate. Rainfall amounts in the 4 to 8 inch range, with locally\nhigher amounts, are possible for all of Chuuk State westward through\nat least eastern Yap State. This could then expand further west\nacross central Yap state over the weekend, dependent on how quickly\n90W strengthens and what track it ends up taking. Locations currently\nto be most affected through early Monday morning include:\n\nGenerally north of 6N:\n\nIn Chuuk State:\nChuuk, Losap, Fananu, Onoun, and Polowat.\n\nIn eastern and Central Yap State (most probable):\nPikelot, West Fayu, Gaferut, Faraulep, Fais, and Ulithi.\n\nIn the remainder of Yap State (possible):\nSatawal, Lamotrek, Olimargo, Ifalik, Eauripik, Sorol, and Yap\nproper.\n\nResidents are urged to pay close attention the next few days to your\nlocal emergency management, the National Weather Service Guam webpage\n(which can be found at www.weather.gov/gum), information put out by\nWeather Service Offices Chuuk and Yap, and our social media pages.",

                "description": "* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.\n\n* WHERE...North and eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and Culebra.\n\n* WHEN...From Thursday morning through late Friday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away\nfrom shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to\nreturn to safety.",
                "instruction": "There is a high risk of rip currents.\n\nRip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away\nfrom shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the\nsandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties\nand piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and\nsigns.\n\nIf you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain\ncalm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for\nhelp.                 "description": "* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip\ncurrents, large breaking waves, and strong longshore currents\nin the surf zone. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking\nwaves of 5 to 9 feet expected in the surf zone.\n\n* WHERE...Ocracoke Island and Core Banks beaches.\n\n* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 11 AM EDT Thursday.\nFor the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and\nlocalized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best\nswimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore\nbreak can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom\ncausing neck and back injuries. Strong longshore currents will\ncreate dangerous swimming conditions.",
                "instruction": "Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to\ndangerous surf conditions.\n\nLife-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain\ncalm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,\nfloat or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to\nescape, face the shore and call or wave for help.\n\nShore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is\nextremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you\nare in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at\nall times.\n\nStrong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip\ncurrents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas.                 "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued April 8 at 7:36PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU",
                "description": "Corrected typos\n\nA tropical disturbance, known as JTWC's Invest 90W, is centered near\n9N154E northeast of Weno, Chuuk. However, the proximity of\nthis system is expected to bring heavier showers, strong winds and\npossibly near gale-force gusts late today and potentially overnight.\nDue to the loose organization of 90W, variability in areas of\nconvective development may produce periods of little to no weather\nfollowed by sporadic heavy showers and thunderstorms. In addition,\nhigh uncertainty remains regarding rainfall amounts, but model trends\nindicate 3 to 5 inches at Weno, Chuuk the next 48 hours, to then\npossibly be higher at outer islands such as Fananu and eastern islands\nof Yap State.
